deductions: "Channel 3 ... Never present in the training data. It is an object type that was defined but never appeared (e.g. a power-up)" (listed among the 'firm conclusions'; fact sheet: channel 3 is the maze walls, always on at 52 cells)
marks.conclusion: A Pac-Man-like policy net on a fixed 10x10 maze; it reads the agent's cell as a flow field, mapping outputs to NOOP/UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT, and circles the outer ring counter-clockwise.
marks.judge_notes: Score: core 16 (A7 B6 C3 D0 E1, minus 1), bonus name 2. Rulings where the rubric did not decide: (1) Border 0: walls were found as cells with noise-level weights in every channel, not as always-on rows that copy the bias. (2) Channel meanings: ch0, ch1 (moving entity) and ch2 (pellets/items) credited although the reply calls ch1/ch2/ch4 educated guesses, because each is a committed reading with a weight-based reason (sparse, strong weights; many cells feeding one unit with the same sign). ch4 'empty floor' was hedged ('possibly'), so earns nothing and no deduction. (3) Action meanings 5/5: the reply derived 0=no-op, 1=up, 2=down, 3=left, 4=right from W1 cluster to W2/W3 tracing plus a legal-move argument; this matches the fact sheet. (4) Depth level 2 not 3: units are traced to outputs, but the fact sheet gives no mechanism to check the 'outer-ring patrol' against. (5) Behaviour 0: 'circle the outer corridor' is not the pellet-chasing, ghost-avoiding behaviour; I did not deduct because the fact sheet does not trace the mechanism and the reply says other channels can override. (6) Training method 1: it argues policy-gradient (or behaviour cloning) from the zero-sum W3 rows and b3, a hedge between RL and imitation; I credited it. (7) Name: 'Pac-Man-like' counted as a commitment to the game/family.
